coreValues.name: Innovation First

coreValues.name: Customer Obsession
coreValues.description: Our customers' success is our success, period

coreFocus.niche: AI-powered workflow automation for mid-market B2B SaaS

eos.tenYearTarget: Become the operating system for automated business processes

icp.avatar: VP of Operations at growing B2B SaaS company
icp.trigger: When manual processes become bottlenecks to growth and the team is drowning in repetitive work
before: Teams spending 20+ hours/week on manual data entry and report generation
Critical business processes breaking down as company scales
Disconnected tools creating data silos and workflow friction
High error rates from manual processes impacting customer experience
after: 80% reduction in manual work with automated intelligent workflows
Real-time visibility into all business processes across departments
Error rates reduced by 95% through AI-powered validation
Team freed up to focus on strategic initiatives instead of busywork
icp.primaryGoals:
1. Automate repetitive manual processes to free up team capacity
2. Gain real-time visibility into all business operations
3. Reduce errors and improve data quality across systems
4. Scale operations without proportional headcount increase
5. Improve customer experience through faster, more reliable processes
icp.secondaryGoals:
1. Reduce operational costs by 30-40%
2. Improve employee satisfaction by eliminating tedious work
3. Enable data-driven decision making
4. Accelerate time-to-market for new initiatives
5. Build competitive advantage through operational excellence
icp.dreams:
1. Fully automated operations that run 24/7 without human intervention
2. Perfect data quality and instant insights across all systems
3. Team focused entirely on innovation and customer value
4. Seamless scaling from 100 to 10,000 customers without operational pain
5. Industry-leading efficiency metrics that attract top talent and investors
icp.promises:
1. 80% reduction in manual work within 90 days of implementation
2. Zero-code workflow automation that business teams can build themselves
3. Enterprise-grade security and compliance without complexity
4. Sub-second performance even at massive scale
5. White-glove onboarding and ongoing optimization support
icp.primaryComplaint:
1. Current automation tools are too complex and require engineering resources
2. Existing workflows break constantly and require constant maintenance
3. Can't trust data quality so still manually verify everything
4. Integration hell - too many disconnected tools and APIs
5. Automation projects take 6-12 months and fail to deliver ROI
icp.secondaryComplaint:
1. High subscription costs for tools that don't deliver promised value
2. Vendor lock-in with platforms that don't integrate well
3. Poor customer support when automation breaks
4. Compliance and security concerns with third-party automation
5. Lack of visibility into what's actually happening in workflows
icp.objections:
1. 'We already have automation tools that we're not fully utilizing'
2. 'Our processes are too complex and unique to be automated'
3. 'We can't afford another tool subscription right now'
4. 'We don't have technical resources to implement and maintain this'
5. 'We've tried automation before and it didn't work'
icp.badHabits:
1. Relying on manual processes and hero employees to keep things running
2. Accepting broken workflows and workarounds as 'good enough'
3. Delaying automation initiatives until problems become critical
4. Underestimating the true cost of manual processes
5. Choosing point solutions instead of platform thinking
icp.consequences:
1. Operational costs spiraling out of control as company scales
2. Critical mistakes impacting customers and revenue
3. Unable to scale without massive hiring which kills margins
4. Best employees leaving due to tedious, repetitive work
5. Competitors gaining advantage through superior operational efficiency
icp.enemy:
1. The belief that 'our business is too unique to be automated'
2. Analysis paralysis delaying automation initiatives
3. Choosing complexity and customization over simplicity and speed
4. Treating automation as IT project instead of business transformation
5. Accepting manual processes as 'just how we do things'
icp.biggestFear:
1. Implementing automation that makes things worse instead of better
2. Losing control over critical business processes
3. Data breaches or compliance violations from third-party tools
4. Team resistance killing adoption and ROI
5. Getting locked into a platform that becomes a limitation

negative: 67% of automation projects fail to deliver expected ROI
Average mid-market company wastes $500K/year on manual processes
73% of employees report spending >20% of time on repetitive tasks
Manual processes have 5-10% error rates on average
Companies lose 20-30% productivity to disconnected tools
general: 80% of successful automation delivers ROI within 6 months
Automated workflows are 95% more accurate than manual processes
Companies with advanced automation grow 2.5x faster than peers
Employees at highly automated companies report 40% higher job satisfaction
Leading companies automate 60-70% of routine operational tasks

pastExperiences.title: RPA Implementation Failure
pastExperiences.whatTried: Implemented traditional RPA tools like UiPath or Automation Anywhere
pastExperiences.whyTried: Promised easy automation of repetitive tasks without coding
pastExperiences.whyFailed: Required constant maintenance, broke with every UI change, needed dedicated RPA developers, cost more than savings

pastExperiences.title: Custom Internal Tools
pastExperiences.whatTried: Built custom automation scripts and internal tools with engineering team
pastExperiences.whyTried: Complete control and customization for unique processes
pastExperiences.whyFailed: Became technical debt nightmare, key employee dependencies, couldn't scale, diverted engineering from product work
